title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
abstract: arXiv:2611.18878v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framework to audit LLM-based recommender systems for structural bias. Candidate descriptions are rewritten by randomly assigned paraphrasing models and presented in random order. We prove that, if the recommender's choice is invariant to these rewritings, every paraphraser is selected with equal probability, yielding a statistical test that requires no relevance labels. translated_title: 通过随机改写实现LLM推荐系统中结构性偏差的无标签检测：以冗长性为例
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）日益被部署为电商和对话式购物系统中的推荐器，它们从一组以自然语言描述的检索候选商品中挑选产品。其决策本应取决于与用户查询的相关性，但也可能受到描述表面属性（如长度）的影响。由于相关性标签很少可用，检测这类结构性偏差十分困难。我们提出了一个无标签框架，用于审计基于LLM的推荐系统中的结构性偏差。候选商品描述由随机分配的改写模型进行改写，并以随机顺序呈现。我们证明，如果推荐器的选择对这些改写保持不变，那么每个改写器被选中的概率相等，由此得到一个无需相关性标签的统计检验。一个四步统计流程用于检验该性质并量化各因素的贡献……
tldr: 提出一种基于随机改写的无标签统计检验框架，无需相关性标签即可检测LLM推荐系统中由文本表面属性（如冗长性）引起的结构性偏差。
en_tdlr: A label-free framework using randomized paraphrasing and a statistical test to detect structural biases (e.g., verbosity) in LLM-based recommender systems without requiring relevance labels.
